newsitem.title: EGYPT: Syrian foreign minister in Cairo to see Mubarak.
newsitem.headline: Syrian foreign minister in Cairo to see Mubarak.

text.p: Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara arrived on Thursday in Cairo, the centre of Arab consultations on the crisis in Middle East peace talks, and went straight into talks with President Hosni Mubarak.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was due later in the day and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was expected to send his foreign policy adviser Dore Gold and perhaps a foreign ministry official to meet Mubarak.
Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri met Mubarak earlier on Thursday but his talks also covered a trade dispute.
Shara said on arrival Netanyahu bore full responsibility for the crisis. Netanyahu has pressed on with a Jewish housing project in Arab East Jerusalem over international protests.

Israel has also proposed bypassing interim Israeli troop withdrawals from the West Bank to complete "final status" talks within six months -- a proposal the Palestinians dismissed as a trick and a publicity stunt.
Shara said: "The demarches that Egypt and Syria are making in Arab and world capitals are to alert international public opinion to the dangers of this period."
Asked if an Arab summit was possible, he said: "Consultations on this subject are under way."
Mubarak had spoken to Netanyahu and Syrian President Hafez al-Assad by telephone in the previous 24 hours.
